Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo earlier. Legal looped me in with the attached redlines (see ClearWave_MSA_redlines_20270416.pdf). High-level points they want clarified before procurement can sign:

1) Output ownership: request that any outputs generated by Redwood using our prompts be explicitly "assigned" to ClearWave for all internal productization. They want sample assignment language in the MSA.
2) Training / model use: they are asking for explicit opt-out — no training on customer data — unless a separate license is agreed.
3) Feedback license: they want a limited license for feedback that allows Redwood to use bug reports and telemetry but not customer content as training data.
4) Evidence & controls: SOC 2 report, retention policy for request logs, and a clause about deletion on termination.

Can you confirm Redwood's standard positions and whether the Order Form can include a narrow carveout for internal model evaluation only? Also attaching the OrderForm_CW_0423.docx they sent.

We can do a quick call Monday if helpful — legal prefers a short redline exchange before countersign.

Best,
Sofia Rivera

Rafael / team — reviewed the PDF and Order Form. High-level legal posture and a suggested compromise below.

Summary of our business constraints:
- We cannot assign model IP or improvements — that breaks our product and business model.
- We can, however, grant broad rights to customer outputs (the text/structured content generated) and a limited, nonexclusive license to use redacted telemetry and bug reports.

Suggested MSA language (start with Option A, fallback Option B):

Option A (preferred compromise):
"Customer owns Generated Outputs produced by Redwood in response to Customer-provided prompts. Redwood retains ownership of its models, model weights, and derived improvements. Redwood may use Aggregated Non-Identifiable Telemetry and anonymized feedback for the purpose of improving service quality, provided that Customer Data and Generated Outputs are not used to train base models or reproduce Customer-Owned Works without Customer's explicit written consent."

Option B (if customer insists on stronger language):
"Customer owns Generated Outputs. Redwood may not use Customer Data or Generated Outputs to train models for production services without a separate written license. Redwood may retain ephemeral, non-identifiable logs for debugging for up to 30 days and shall provide SOC2 evidence upon reasonable request."

Training opt-out approach: allow a clear checkbox in the Order Form: "No training on my data (production)." If selected, Redwood will not use Customer Data or Generated Outputs for model training except for internal, ephemeral evaluation described in the Order Form (e.g., up to 30 days, aggregated, anonymized). Provide an escalations path to purchase a training license.

Feedback license: provide a narrow clause that permits Redwood to use customer-submitted feedback, bug reports, and anonymized telemetry to improve the service (no model weight training on raw customer content).

Evidence: provide current SOC2 report and high-level retention policy. We should attach SOC2_snapshot_202703.zip. Also propose a short "evidence addendum" that lists what we will share (report PDF, retention summary) under an NDA.

Commercial trade: Ben / Priyom — recommend offering a limited pilot credit or a 2-month free Evaluation Tier in exchange for accepting Option A. That will address procurement optics.

If we agree, I'll produce a redline to the MSA and a single-line Order Form checkbox entry for the opt-out.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
